what: PER-GROUP FLATS — does narrowing the flat window from 500 frames to 100 pay, and where?
uptime: 16:27:45 up 38 days, 38 min,  2 users,  load average: 16.15, 9.63, 6.92
sign_convention: delivered armB/armA = flat_A/flat_B = set/g_k, the INVERSE of the flat-to-flat ratio g_k/set. The comparison windows are built in the delivered orientation.

floor_group_depth.pair: two flats from INTERLEAVED halves of ONE group (50 + 50)
floor_group_depth.why: both halves span the same sub-burst, so any time-evolving term cancels and only the build floor remains

compose_level_cancellation.reading: the mean of the five per-group departures is under 1% of the typical departure on BOTH axes, so a plain-mean compose of five members cancels over 99% of the correction to first order. This is the per-set flat being the groups' own average, confirmed by measurement. A null at the COMPOSED level is therefore a PREDICTED result and is NOT a null for per-group flats — the gain, if there is one, is a per-MEMBER gain, and the member is the cross-night combine unit.
compose_level_cancellation.corollary_on_the_object_tilt_axis: the L/R slope — the axis the object tilt lives on — swings across the groups while its mean vanishes, so a per-member L/R calibration error is invisible in the composed mean precisely because it cancels. Sizes against the stack's own +0.171 %/1000px sensor-fixed L/R residual are reported in the experiment record; the comparison is licensed by the differential's measured ~1:1 transfer, not assumed.

flat_to_flat.SCOPE_of_the_linear_window_model: The model takes the sweep MAGNITUDE as measured input (the inherited half-to-half term) and predicts only the within-set SHAPE — where each window's mean sits in the burst. It does NOT predict magnitude from duration, and it must never be cited as though it did: that is the REGISTERED DEAD time-dose hypothesis, falsified on its own pre-registered falsifier (set-04 ran 777 s against set-03's 1497 s, so a time-driven term predicted 0.52x; it measured 1.200x). A close agreement here is evidence the SHAPE is smooth and the anchor reproduces, and nothing whatever about predicting a flat term from a burst's length.

card_definitions.role: synthetic FIXTURES divided into the per-set flat by Siril; never delivered, never a calibration frame outside these control arms

prediction_committed_before_the_arms.1_SHAPE_AND_SIGN: flat_gk / flat_set departs with OPPOSITE SIGN at k=1 and k=5 and is smallest in magnitude at k=3. FALSIFIER: the same sign at both ends, or |k=3| not the smallest of the five.
prediction_committed_before_the_arms.2_MAGNITUDE: under a linear-in-window-position model calibrated on the inherited half-to-half 3.481% (window midpoints at 10/30/50/70/90% of the burst against the halves' 25/75%): |g1 vs set| = |g5 vs set| = 2.78% corner spread, |g2| = |g4| = 1.39%, |g3| ~ 0, and |g1 vs g5| = 5.57% = 1.6x the half-to-half term. Accepted within a factor 1.5 either way. FALSIFIER: |g1 vs set| < 1.0%, which would mean the group windows are not materially different from the set mean and the item is moot.
prediction_committed_before_the_arms.3_MONOTONICITY: the signed statistic is monotone in group order across all five, if a smooth within-burst evolution is the driver. FALSIFIER: a non-monotone excursion exceeding 3x the measured floor.
prediction_committed_before_the_arms.4_AXIS: T/B dominant: |y-slope| / |x-slope| > 3 on the group-to-set ratios (11.6x on the half-split). IF IT COMES OUT L/R DOMINANT THE ATTRIBUTION IS WRONG AND THAT IS THE FINDING. Either way this does not speak to the object's L/R tilt, which stays UNTESTED.
prediction_committed_before_the_arms.5_FLOOR: the 50+50 interleaved floor scales as sqrt(250/50) = 2.24x the inherited 250+250 figure -> ~0.078% corner spread, and in any case below 0.35%, leaving the smallest group effect >= 10x above it. FALSIFIER: the floor exceeds one third of the smallest group-vs-set effect.
prediction_committed_before_the_arms.6_DELIVERED_TRANSFER: ~1:1 at member level, per the flat differential's measured 0.9887 raw / 1.0117 corrected by the planted control against a floor of exactly zero: the delivered edge dipole of arm B member k over arm A member k equals the two flats' own ratio measured over the delivered canvas, within 0.99-1.01 after the planted correction. FALSIFIER: below 0.5x or above 1.5x.
prediction_committed_before_the_arms.7_COMPOSED_LEVEL_CANCELLATION: THE SHARPEST NEW PREDICTION, and it is a warning about where the payoff is NOT. The compose is a plain mean of five members, so the composed arms differ by the MEAN of the five per-group corrections — which prediction 1's antisymmetry drives to approximately zero. Predicted: |composed difference| < 1/3 of the mean |member-level| difference. If it holds, per-group flats fix MEMBERS and barely move the per-set composed product; the member is the cross-night combine unit, so the payoff would live at the combine, not at this stack. FALSIFIER: the composed difference is comparable to the member-level difference.
prediction_committed_before_the_arms.8_MEMBER_TO_MEMBER_RISK: the brief names the risk that per-group flats reduce every member's own residual while making members differ MORE from each other. Two mechanisms compete: (a) each member gets the flat matched to its own window, so the low-order calibration residual per member shrinks and members should agree MORE; (b) a 100-frame flat averages 90.9 px of celestial motion against the set flat's 453.3 px, so it bakes in MORE sky-fixed structure, and a different one per group. Predicted: (a) dominates the low-order term the differential measures — arm B's member-to-member low-order spread is at or below arm A's. FALSIFIER: arm B's spread exceeds arm A's.
prediction_committed_before_the_arms.9_ENABLING_CONDITION: build_sky_flat.sh's stated enabling condition is drift exceeding ~20-100 px across the frames a flat is built from. The set flat gets 453.3 px; a 100-frame group gets 90.9 px — INSIDE the stated band but at its boundary. Predicted: the group flats show a higher findstar speck count than the set flat's 1 (the builder's own residual-sky check). FALSIFIER: speck counts unchanged, which would mean the narrower window costs nothing in baked-in structure.
